panels.description: Soonest-expiring cert across all probed endpoints. cert-manager renews at 30 days out; yellow means renewal is late

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: All 3 shared vCPUs together

panels.title: CPU steal
panels.description: Time a noisy Hetzner neighbor took from our shared vCPUs. Sustained >10% means resize or move

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: 4 GB total; every tenant daemon eats into this

panels.title: Disk used
panels.description: Root disk full kills the k3s datastore; tenant volume full stops every sync

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: 3 vCPUs, so sustained load above 3 is saturation

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Public interface. Sync bursts are normal; a flat line during business hours is not

panels.title: Container restarts (per hour)
panels.description: Empty is the healthy state — any line here is a crash loop or OOM cycle

panels.title: Memory by pod (top 10)
panels.description: Working set — what the OOM killer judges

panels.title: CPU by pod (top 10)
panels.description: In cores; the node has 3

panels.title: Unhealthy signals
panels.description: Both flat at zero when healthy

targets.expr: sum(kube_pod_status_ready{condition="false"} unless on(namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Succeeded"} == 1)) OR on() vector(0)

panels.title: cert-manager: days to expiry
panels.description: passband-wildcard (DNS-01) and warden (HTTP-01). Renewal fires at 30 days; a line sinking below 30 means renewal is failing — check the Cloudflare token first

panels.title: Traefik requests
panels.description: Everything entering the box over 80/443

panels.title: Tenant pods running
panels.description: One pod per tenant. The Google-verification cap is 100

panels.title: Tenant memory
panels.description: Per tenant daemon

panels.title: Tenant CPU
panels.description: Per tenant daemon, in cores

panels.title: Tenant PVC usage
panels.description: Per-tenant mailbox volumes on the shared 50 GB block volume

panels.title: Tenant restarts (per hour)
panels.description: Empty is healthy. A restarting tenant daemon is a tenant not getting mail triaged

panels.title: Sync staleness
panels.description: Seconds since that tenant's last successful Gmail sync. The panel this row exists for: a pod can be Running, ready, and completely stuck, and nothing outside the daemon can tell. One line climbing is usually that tenant's Google credential; every line climbing is the box. Alert on 15m.

panels.title: Gmail API errors
panels.description: By kind, per tenant. Empty is healthy. Rate-limit and transient kinds come in bursts and heal themselves; an auth spike does not. A tenant throwing auth errors has a dead refresh token, and no amount of restarting the pod fixes it: that tenant has to re-consent with Google.

panels.title: LLM spend (24h)
panels.description: Rolling 24 hours of stage-2 triage spend, per tenant. The number worth comparing it against is that tenant's configured daily cap; the colours here are a generous default, not the cap.

panels.title: Store on disk
panels.description: The daemon's own view of its SQLite footprint, database and WAL summed. Tenant PVC usage above is the volume's view of the same bytes; the two drifting apart is usually a WAL that stopped checkpointing.

panels.title: Triage throughput
panels.description: Verdicts per second across the fleet, by stage and outcome. Flat at zero while mail is arriving means triage is not running at all. A stage-2 share that climbs means the heuristics stopped catching the easy cases, and the spend panel follows it within the hour.
